q1.prompt: Redirect is the dominant URL-shortener query and always knows code. Which shard key keeps that read on one shard?

choices.label: A hash of code, routed to the shard that owns its logical bucket
A random value generated independently for every read

wrong1.prompt: Routing must be reproducible from the access key.
wrong1.explanation: The same code must always resolve to the shard that stores its row. A random read key cannot route without a full directory or scatter-gather.

q2.prompt: Why map 256 logical buckets onto 8 physical primaries instead of storing at hash(code) % 8 forever?

choices.label: Adding a ninth primary can move selected buckets instead of remapping most rows
Logical buckets guarantee that no key can ever become hot

wrong2.explanation: Changing a direct modulo from 8 to 9 changes the destination for most hashes. A bucket map lets operators move controlled ranges; it does not eliminate skew.

q3.prompt: One viral code receives 50,000 reads/s. Will changing the shard hash spread that single row across all primaries?

choices.label: No. Cache and replicate the hot value; one key still routes together
Yes. Any hash automatically divides one key over every shard

wrong3.prompt: Sharding does not split one hot key.
wrong3.explanation: A deterministic shard key keeps all access to the same row together. Hot-record reads need caching or replicas, not a different modulo.

success.prompt: You chose a routable shard key, planned rebalancing, and handled a hot record separately.
